source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
The CyrusOne San Antonio campus publishes 33 MW of IT capacity across two facilities, but no published fact shows whether any of that power is dedicated to AI training or serving regulated enterprise workloads.

At 40 kW per rack, 33 MW would support roughly 825 racks, or about 6,600 accelerator slots at eight accelerators per rack. The operator does not state actual rack density or accelerator count, so this is an estimate, not a deployment figure.

The campus ranks sixth among the nineteen Texas facilities that publish power capacity, holding 6.9% of the state's disclosed 475 MW. But Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, and only nineteen publish capacity, so the rank reflects disclosure, not true market position.

Certifications include SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISMA, TIA-942, and HITRUST. These qualify the campus for regulated enterprise, healthcare, and federal workloads, but none is specific to AI. No data is published on grid interconnection, power source, allocation, or GPU deployment, so this campus cannot be assessed as a binding constraint on AI scaling.
